reasons.A: Smooth, even modern sentences and an explanatory, essayistic stance; it lacks the passage's chatty oddity, reported-speech drollery and abrupt short paragraphs.
reasons.B: Short, varied sentences, deadpan irony, snippets of the landlady's reported speech and tiny one-line paragraphs come closest to the passage's dry, anecdotal movement.
reasons.C: Catches the confiding 'you' and the 'curious thing' tone, but its long, balanced sentences, semicolons and extended customs metaphor are more polished and literary than the author's loose, talky manner.
